The shot image; omitted when the shot has no accepted asset yet (runner shows a placeholder).
A character speaks (dialogue or parenthetical).
Speaking character id (a key into {@link Playable.characters}).
Un-attributed narration or action.
A single ordered beat within a scene.
A branch edge in the playable (mirrors {@link Choice}).
A character as the runner needs it: display name + optional portrait.
One scene, flattened into ordered beats plus its outgoing edges.
Linear continuation, followed when `choices` is empty.
The whole playable story.
Entry scene id.

Draw the speaking character's portrait over the shot image. Defaulted rather than optional
so every consumer reads a plain boolean, and a file written before the field still parses.

The chunk model behind an editable image prompt (`docs/plans/archive/chunked-prompts.md`).

A prompt is still a flat string everywhere it matters — `TaskInputs.*.prompt` is inside the task
hash, so it cannot become structured without re-keying every task in every project. Chunks are
the authoring view of the same string: each builder's array of clauses, made addressable, with
`renderPrompt` collapsing them exactly as the builders always did.

The shapes live here rather than in `@vn/artgen` because the entity types that store an
override are here too, and the two copies would drift apart if the type were declared twice.
What a chunk contributes. Used only for the tag on its card.

Where a chunk's words came from — an address a surface can open, not a position. `builder` is
the one origin with no document behind it: the scaffolding sentences the builders write.
An `art.setNotes` address, e.g. `character:aiko` or `shot:arrival/arrival__a`.
A concept's authored sentence.
Scaffolding — no document behind it.
One clause of a derived prompt, addressable by {@link PromptChunk.key}.

Stable across re-derivation — an override is keyed by it. Derived from the origin address,
never from position or text, so editing art notes keeps the override attached.
The sentence this chunk contributes, already punctuated.

A second rung that fed the same sentence, when the builder folded two into one (the outfit
inside a model sheet's subject line, or an entity note beside a narrower rung). Purely
presentational: a card can name the rung a word came from without splitting the chunk, which
would change the prompt.

Authored text plus the derived text it was written against. `of` is what lets a replacement be
carried forward: when the derivation underneath moves, the old text, the new text and the
author's replacement together are enough to rewrite it. An absent `of` means unknown, not stale.
sha256 of the chunk's derived text when this was written.
An agent-condensed whole prompt, held in place until it is recondensed.

`chunkFingerprint` of the chunk list this condensed. A mismatch means the text is held in
place rather than treated as stale.
ISO timestamp of the condensation.

The logical slot a linked reference was resolved from — never a hash, because the point of a
binding is to survive the slot's contents changing. `asset` is the degenerate case: a concept or
an upload has no slot behind it, so the hash identifies it and it can never drift.

A reference image attached to one chunk — evidence for that clause, so muting the clause drops
its references too.

The pin is what reaches `TaskInputs.refs` and therefore the task hash, so nothing re-renders on
its own when the slot underneath moves. Drift is computed on read as
`resolveBinding(from) !== pin`. A ref with no {@link from} is a custom upload: there is no slot
to compare against, so it can never drift.
Asset hash of the bytes actually fed to the model.

An author's override of one derived prompt, stored at the rung that names the whole picture.
Everything here is optional and nothing has a default, so an override with no content
serializes to no key at all. Otherwise every sheet would grow an empty block on its first edit.
Chunk keys to drop. A muted chunk contributes no text and no references.
Partial order of chunk keys. Unlisted keys follow, in derivation order.
`mode === 'custom'`: sent verbatim, trimmed only.
Reference images, by chunk key, in authored order.

Provider-agnostic generative interfaces (report §8, §P6, §P7). The scheduler never
imports a concrete provider — it only knows Task/deps/status. Providers are swapped
via model ids in project.yaml.
Result of an image generation or edit.
Raw image bytes.
Seed actually used, when the provider reports one.
Generates and edits images (Gemini "nano banana" in practice).
Reference-guided edit: variants, outfits, time-of-day re-lights.
Severity of a defect found by a vision reviewer.
A single defect in a structured critique (report §P7).
Targeted prompt edit suggested to fix it.
Structured critique of one generated image.
Who produced this review, e.g. `gemini` or `claude`.
What a shot is supposed to depict; handed to reviewers as the spec (report §P7).
Reads an image back and reports defects against the spec (Gemini and Claude).
Stable id, e.g. `gemini` or `claude`.
Text LLM for mining, decomposition, and prompt refinement (report §8).
Free-form completion.

Structured completion: the result is validated against `schema` (a parse fn that
throws on mismatch) with retries. Keeps machine-consumed output well-formed.
Bundle of providers resolved from config and handed to the pipeline.

Zod schemas for every file shape and every machine-consumed LLM result (report §3,
§12). Validating at the boundary keeps malformed front-matter and malformed model
output from leaking into the deterministic core.

The front-matter key that names what an authored document is, so an entity can be found by
content rather than by where it was filed. Named once here and imported everywhere, because a
string literal at a call site lets the reader and the writer disagree about the key.

The document kinds the tag can name. A file in `characters/`/`locations/` carries its tag
implicitly from its location; stating a different one there is a conflict, not an override.

One authored chunk edit. The bare-string form is what nearly every edit is; the object form
carries `of`, the derived text the edit was written against, so a later change underneath can be
carried forward rather than silently orphaning the author's words.

The slot a linked reference was resolved from. `.strict()` per member, so a misspelled address
is a parse error rather than a binding that silently resolves to nothing and reads as drift.

One reference image on one chunk. A ref with no `from` is an upload: there is no slot behind it,
so it cannot drift.

An author's override of one derived image prompt (`docs/plans/archive/chunked-prompts.md`). Stored at
the rung that names the whole picture, so "which override applies" is a lookup, never a merge.

Nothing in here carries a `.default()`. A default would make `compact()` keep an empty
`prompt_override` key on every sheet's first edit, which is the failure the wardrobe's
`synthesized` check already exists to prevent. `.strict()` for the same reason `outfitEntry` is:
a misspelled key would silently drop an override from a prompt.

The written form of a chunk edit → the in-memory one. Written once here because two readers
(`@vn/model`'s entity docs and `@vn/store`'s shots file) both parse an override, and a second
copy of this mapping could drop an author's `of` in one of them.
Chunk keys whose reference list is empty carry no meaning, so they are never written.
Drop the keys the override did not set, so a written override never grows an empty block.
Parsed front matter → the in-memory {@link PromptOverride}.

The inverse. An edit that records no `of` is written back as the bare string it was read from,
which is what keeps a hand-authored `replace: { subject: '…' }` looking the way it was written.

Whether an override would change nothing. `mode` alone is not an override — it names which of
the three shapes is in force, and all three fall back to the derived chunks when the shape they
name is empty. Writers use this to clear the key rather than grow an inert `prompt_override:` on
every sheet that was ever edited.

An authored image seed, at any rung that carries one. Non-negative and whole because that is
what an image backend takes; a fractional or negative seed is a typo, and coercing it would
quietly draw a different picture than the one written down.

The long form of a wardrobe entry or a location variant: what it is, plus how it should look.
`.strict()` because a misspelled key here would silently drop art direction from a prompt.
Front-matter of a character sheet — `characters/<id>/character.md`, or any `type: character`.
Optional in the conventional directory, which carries the tag implicitly.

The character's wardrobe, outfit id → description, in the order written. The description is
what a prompt says the character is wearing; an id with no entry falls back to saying the id.
`default_outfit` need not appear — it is synthesized when the map omits it.

An outfit that carries art direction of its own is written as an object instead; the string
form is kept because it is what nearly every wardrobe needs and what every sheet already has.
Free-form art direction appended to every prompt this character reaches.
Image seed for every prompt this character reaches; an outfit entry's own seed is narrower.
Overrides the derived portrait prompt. A sheet's override lives on its outfit entry.
Front-matter of a set-location sheet — `locations/<id>.md`, or any `type: location`.

The variants plates are generated for, in the order written. A bare string is the id alone;
a variant that describes itself or carries art direction is written as an object.
Free-form art direction appended to every plate of this location.
Image seed for every plate of this location; a variant entry's own seed is narrower.

Front-matter of `scenes/<id>.md` — the scene's identity and nothing else. Every other
field (heading, location, synopsis, choices, next, line ids) lives in the Fountain body,
where `splitScenes` reads it and `sceneToFountain` writes it back losslessly; a
front-matter copy would be a second source of truth for a field that already has one.
Hence `.strict()`: an unrecognized key is an error, not a silently ignored line.
Must equal the filename stem; `@vn/model` reports a mismatch rather than picking one.
`project.yaml` (report §8, §11).

The entry scene's id. Optional here rather than required, because a project missing it is
reported as an error diagnostic by the model, which can list the available scene ids where
this schema cannot. A project that has not been imported yet has no scene ids to choose from.
Env var names that hold API keys; never the keys themselves.

Total run-level attempts at a task before the scheduler stops requeueing it, so the
default of 2 is one retry. Orthogonal to `max_refine_attempts`, which caps P7's
critique→refine loop within a single run of one shot task.

Draw the speaking character's portrait over the shot image in a runner. Off by default
because a shot prompt names its own subjects, so the frame already contains them and an
overlay is the same character twice. Turning it on stages the classic
background-plus-sprite look — but against a P3 portrait, which is an opaque plate and not
a keyed cutout (docs/plans/archive/portrait-overlay-opt-in.md).
Structured critique returned by a vision reviewer (report §P7).
Locations mined from the screenplay by the LLM (report §P1).
Absent means inherit — see {@link ShotSubject.outfit}. A default would defeat inheritance.
Shots proposed for one scene by the LLM (report §P5).
A parsed decomposition — what the model answers, and what `write_storyboard` restates.

One prompt condensed from a chunk list by the LLM (`docs/plans/archive/chunked-prompts.md` §4).

`omitted` is what the model reports it could not fit. It is advisory and nothing rejects a
condensation over it — the authoritative answer is the local coverage check run over `prompt`.

The derived half of a persisted shot: what a run produced, never what a human authored.
Rewritten wholesale on every run from the task graph and the manifest, which remain the
authority — this is a readable copy, not an input. Absent means "not run yet".
P6, rebuilt by `buildShotPrompt` from the authored fields.
P7 output asset hash; `manifest.json` is the authority for the bytes.

Hash of the covered lines' text when `image` was produced, so a later load can tell that the
frame no longer illustrates what the scene says. Recorded with the bytes and never refreshed
without them — a rerun that reports the same image must not clear a drift the author has not
acted on. Absent means unknown, and that is how every shot rendered before this field reads.

`work/shots/<sceneId>.json` — one scene's decomposition, persisted so a run reuses it
instead of re-decomposing (the LLM path is non-deterministic, and re-decomposing would
change shot ids, hence task identities, hence regenerate art for no reason).

Everything outside `shotData` is authored and is what a later run compares against.

High-water mark for hand-allocated `<sceneId>__shot<n>` ids — the `Scene.nextLineId`
posture. A shot's id is in its task hash, so re-minting a retired id would resolve to an
already-done task and silently inherit the deleted shot's frame; the mark only ever rises.
Absent on decomposed and pre-mark files, where it is derived by scanning existing ids.
Authored art direction for this frame; in the prompt, so editing it re-renders it.
Authored image seed for this frame; in the task hash, so editing it re-renders it.

The author's override of this frame's derived prompt. Authored, so it sits at top level
beside `artNotes` and never inside `shotData`, which a run rewrites wholesale.

One recorded image-model response in the fixture asset cache. Provenance in the same
spirit as `manifest.json`: enough to see what was asked for, of which model, and when —
so a stale or orphaned entry can be recognized without replaying the request.
`requestKey`: sha256 over the operation, prompt, ordered ref-byte hashes, and params.
The model that actually produced these bytes. `params.modelId` is part of `key`.
sha256 of each reference image's bytes, in the order they were sent.
ISO date of the recording.
The fixture whose run produced it, when the recorder knows.
`index.json` of a fixture asset cache; the bytes live beside it as `<key>.<ext>`.

The task model (report §7). A Task is a unit of generative work whose identity is
a content hash of everything that determines its output — this is what gives the
pipeline dedupe, resumability, and staleness/invalidation for free.
Per-kind, fully-specified inputs. Everything here is folded into the task hash.
A single execution attempt, recorded for provenance (report §P7).
Asset hash produced this attempt, if any.
Structured review verdicts gathered this attempt.
ISO timestamp; stamped by the caller (scripts have no clock).
A node in the task graph. Identity == `hash`.
Upstream task hashes (DAG edges).
Asset hash when done.
Why the task reached a terminal non-`done` state (`failed` or `needs_human`).
A loosely-typed task usable in heterogeneous collections.

Skips rather than throws, so one line written by a newer build does not cost the author every
other line in the log. `@vn/store`'s `readShots` throws for the opposite reason — see its doc

The fields below all live in the Fountain body. Accepting a front-matter copy of one would
give that field two locations and two writers; scene-chunk-files.md picks the body
Fable thinks unconditionally, so `none` has to become the cheapest level it takes.

Which text models the authoring surfaces offer, and what reasoning each of them will accept.
This lives here rather than in `@vn/providers` because both the `vnauthor` REPL and the desktop
renderer need the same answers, and only one of the two can import a package that loads a
vendor SDK.
The effort levels a surface may offer, in order. A tuple, so a command prop can name it.

Reasoning-effort level (Anthropic `output_config.effort`). Higher levels think more and
spend more tokens. Not every model takes every level — ask {@link effortChoicesFor}.

What a surface may bind, weakest first. `none` is thinking switched off — a state, not an
`output_config.effort` value, and the request that carries it sends `thinking: disabled`
instead of an effort.

The choice every surface starts at. Deliberately a level rather than the absence of one: on
Opus 4.7/4.8 and Sonnet 4.6 a request with no `thinking` field runs with no thinking at all,

Curated text models offered by the `/model` menu and the convo pane; any id also works.
`xhigh` arrived on Opus 4.7; the models before it step from `high` straight to `max`.

What a model's effort menu offers, weakest first. Empty means no knob at all: `output_config
.effort` 400s on Haiku 4.5, Sonnet 4.5 and earlier, and the Gemini backend passes none.

`none` is absent where an explicit `thinking: disabled` is refused — Fable/Mythos 5 think
unconditionally and 400 on it.

The choice a model will actually honour. Returns the requested choice when the model offers it,
otherwise the nearest weaker choice it does offer, falling back to its weakest choice when
nothing weaker exists, and `undefined` when it offers no choices at all.

A stored choice outlives the model that offered it: picking `xhigh` on Opus 4.8 and switching to
Sonnet 4.6 leaves a level the new model will not take. The setting is deliberately kept across a
switch, so it is stepped down here rather than refused.
How a choice reads in a menu. `none` reads as `no thinking`, a state rather than a level.
Whether a model honours a reasoning setting at all — what a surface greys out on.

Whether a model accepts a `{"role": "system"}` message inside `messages[]`. Such a message files
turn-scoped truth (the plan/execute mode, a section of the system prompt that has since been
rewritten) without recomposing the cached prefix.

The predicate is model-level rather than backend-level because all four curated Claude entries go
through the same `createAnthropicChat`. An unsupported model answers `role 'system' is not
supported on this model`, and the caller down-renders to a `user` turn instead. That matters most
on a mid-session model switch, which keeps the transcript.
Typed error hierarchy so callers can branch on failure class (report §10).
Bad input: malformed front-matter, dangling goto, invalid config.

A provider call failed terminally: a content refusal, a malformed request, an unusable
reference image. Another attempt returns the same failure and costs the same as the first.
{@link RetryableProviderError} is the transient case.

A provider call failed in a way another attempt could plausibly fix — a 429, a 5xx, a dropped
connection. Only the backend can tell a retryable failure from a terminal one, since it is the
layer that sees the status code; everything above branches on this class.

How long the provider asked us to wait before trying again, in milliseconds, taken from its
own `retry-after` header when it sent one. Absent means the provider named no delay, and every
vendor's guidance in that case is to back off exponentially.
Structured model output could not be parsed/validated after retries.
Configuration problem: missing key, unreadable project.yaml.
Ensure a directory exists (recursive, idempotent).

Atomic write: write to a temp sibling then rename, so a crash never leaves a
half-written file (report §10 crash-safety).

The suffix is random rather than derived from the path and the data's length, because two
writers of the same path with same-length data shared one temp file and raced. The temp is
unlinked in a `finally` so that a failed rename does not leave a `.tmp-…` sibling in `scenes/`,
where a directory listing shows it alongside the scenes. An error from that unlink is ignored,
so a failed cleanup cannot mask the failure that caused it.

On Windows the destination may be held open for a moment by something that scans files as
they change — antivirus, an indexer, an editor's watcher — and the rename then fails EPERM
(or EACCES/EBUSY) even though nothing is wrong with either path. The lock is released in
milliseconds, so a failed rename is retried briefly before it is allowed to be an error.
Append one JSON record as a line to a JSONL file, creating it if needed.
Read a JSONL file into an array of parsed records; missing file → [].
Read a UTF-8 text file.
True if a path exists.
sha256 of bytes or a string, hex-encoded. The content-addressing primitive.

Canonical, stable JSON used for hashing structured inputs: object keys are sorted
recursively so logically-equal inputs always serialize identically.
Hash an ordered list of named parts into a single content-address.
Minimal structured logger writing one JSON-ish line per event to stderr.
Create a logger; level defaults from `VNGEN_LOG` (debug|info|warn|error).

Bounded async pool (report §7, §10): run async tasks with a hard concurrency cap,
preserving input order in the result array. The scheduler uses this to respect a
configurable concurrency limit while running independent tasks in parallel.

Retry an async op with exponential backoff. Throws the last error on exhaustion, and
immediately when `shouldRetry` rules an error out — the default retries everything.

`delayFor` reads a wait out of the failure itself, typically a `retry-after`. A number from it
is used in place of the computed backoff, because a provider that names a delay is reporting
when its own limit resets: a shorter wait gets another 429 and a longer one wastes the
difference.

A rename onto a directory fails, so the temp is written and the rename does not happen,
which is the case the `finally` cleans up after

On Windows antivirus or a watcher holds the destination open for a few milliseconds and
the rename comes back EPERM, though both paths are fine

Same path, same data length is the case the old sha1(path + length) suffix collided on,
where one writer's rename moved the shared temp file out from under the other
A function that rejects with `err` until `succeedAt`, counting its calls.
The predicate exists so that a failure another attempt cannot fix costs only one attempt
